problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡3x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{3}?$
worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{\pi }{18}+\frac{n\pi }{3} \\ x & =\frac{(1+6n)\pi }{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{18}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{18}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{13\pi }{18}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ (written in ascending order) are 

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{18},\frac{7\pi }{18},\frac{13\pi }{18}.
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3} & =\frac{\pi }{18}+\frac{13\pi }{18} \\  & =\frac{14\pi }{18} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
